text:
maria: Quick flag — console needs better per-route telemetry granularity so we can show quota/cost breakdowns. Proposal: SDKs surface a telemetry mode and emit a header. Thinking `x-rw-telemetry-mode: full|summary|lite` as opt-in. Any immediate risks with defaults or proxies?
jon: Prefer opt-in default to avoid storage blowup. 'summary' seems reasonable as a long-term default. Do we have perf numbers for 'full'?
kevin: Perf numbers: 'full' adds ~0.5ms/request on our py/go clients at 128-token avg. Backend storage and billable events increase a lot. My recommendation: SDK default = 'lite' (or no header), console default = 'summary' for visibility, and allow route-level overrides.
lina: From Console UX POV we can show a 'Telemetry mode' per-tenant with an estimated cost delta. Need to avoid header names that proxies strip. Also want a clear tooltip explaining what 'full' contains vs 'lite'.
sam: Go SDK concern: many infra proxies strip unknown headers. We already use `x-rw-routehint`. If we add `x-rw-telemetry-mode` some requests may lose it. Do we consider a fallback header name or duplicating into `x-rw-telemetry` for older proxies? Also, if we change header semantics later, we may need a major version bump.
eva: Py SDK can be conservative: introduce client param `telemetry_mode=None` and env var `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE`. If None, preserve current behavior (no header). If set, emit header. That avoids surprising users.
jon: What about emitting both a new canonical header and a short legacy header for a transition window? e.g., `x-rw-telemetry-mode: full` and also `x-rw-telemetry: full` so proxies that match either will carry it.
maria: Draft rollout plan:
1) Introduce canonical header `x-rw-telemetry-mode` in backend and SDKs (opt-in only).
2) Console rollout: enable 'summary' globally, enable 'full' for a 5% canary.
3) After 8 weeks of monitoring, flip SDK default to 'summary' in a minor release (opt-out possible).
4) If we ever change header semantics (format), we do a major SDK bump.
Questions: telemetry TTL in storage? dashboard tiles to add?
kevin: Agree with plan. Also propose adding a sampling token for correlated traces: `x-rw-telemetry-sample: 0.37` or a lightweight id. Example header block:
```
x-rw-telemetry-mode: full
x-rw-telemetry-sample: abc123
```
Backend will parse both.
lina: For dashboard tiles: add a 'Telemetry mode' filter and show estimated cost impact per mode. UX copy suggestions: "Full: detailed prompt + response metadata (higher cost). Summary: token counts + latency. Lite: only token counts, minimal metadata." Include a modal with sample data rows so customers know what changes.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for console-telemetry-v2 to 5% of tenants (maria) at 2026-06-01T09:32Z
sam: Re: Go SDK header-stripping — duplication seems safest. Plan: emit both `x-rw-telemetry-mode` and `x-rw-telemetry` for a 12-week window, log at debug when telemetry enabled, and add a compatibility test that runs requests through our internal proxy to ensure headers survive.
eva: I'll open a py PR today. Implementation notes: env var `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE`, client kwarg `telemetry_mode='full'|'summary'|'lite'`, unit tests to assert header presence only when set. Also add docs in Quickstart about cost implications.
jon: For quotas: if `telemetry_mode=full` map usage to quota_bucket `telemetry_full` so billing & quota attribution are clear. Otherwise use `default` bucket. We should document this in the billing/quotas page and include an alert if a tenant flips to 'full' and is approaching quota.
maria: I'll draft the rollout doc & canary checklist. Owners: sam (Go), eva (Py), kevin (Platform infra), lina (Console). Target: minor SDK releases in ~4 weeks; console canary is live now. Ping me if objections. :thumbsup:
